    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • Industry observers note that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • Sources indicate that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Industry observers note that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    Sources indicate that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Sources indicate that transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Lions score touchdown to end first half after Dan Campbell opts for safety on Bears' illegal batting penalty

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (541 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the high-powered Thanksgiving matchup between the Detroit Lions and the Chicago Bears delivered early, with a wild sequence just before halftime.
    • Though potentially a game-changing opportunity, the sequence wasn't enough to get the win: After a high-scoring second half, Chicago eventually pulled off a stunning 39-35 win off a last-second touchdown.
    • The Lions' late first-half sequence started after the two-minute warning, with quarterback Caleb Williams getting sacked and fumbling the ball at the Bears' 2-yard line.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the high-powered Thanksgiving matchup between the Detroit Lions and the Chicago Bears delivered early, with a wild sequence just before halftime. After accepting a potentially risky safety on an unusual Bears penalty, the Lions converted a touchdown to close out the first half with a 19-10 lead.

    Though potentially a game-changing opportunity, the sequence wasn't enough to get the win: After a high-scoring second half, Chicago eventually pulled off a stunning 39-35 win off a last-second touchdown.

    The Lions' late first-half sequence started after the two-minute warning, with quarterback Caleb Williams getting sacked and fumbling the ball at the Bears' 2-yard line.

    Once out of Williams' hands, the ball bounced past multiple players into the Chicago end zone. Bears offensive lineman Darnell Wright, in an effort to stave off a safety, used a close fist to bat the ball out of the end zone, where Lions defensive back Brian Branch was able to get his hands on it.

    But Wright's efforts to get the ball out of the end zone were not allowed: The lineman was flagged for "illegal batting," which results in a safety if the foul occurs in the end zone.

    The situation presented Lions head coach Dan Campbell with a decision: Take the safety and try to put together a touchdown drive before halftime, or decline the penalty to get the ball and set up a red-zone drive.

    Campbell decided to go for the safety, giving him and the Lions a minute and change to grab a touchdown and justify the choice.

    Initially, the drive got off to a concerning start: The Lions, who had already been called for two false starts earlier in the quarter, picked up two more false start penalties in a row to set up third-and-12. Jared Goff then erased some of the distance by finding Jahmyr Gibbs for an 11-yard reception, but the catch fell just short of first down.

    On fourth-and-1, though, Detroit pulled off a gutsy and successful quarterback sneak, giving Goff the 2-yard rush to keep the drive going. That set up a massive 39-yard throw from Goff to Jameson Williams, before another first down to Gibbs, and a successful touchdown throw to Sam LaPorta.

    Sources indicate that in an interview on the broadcast after halftime, Campbell told CBS that the number of timeouts left — the Bears had two at the time, while the Lions had all three — and his faith in his players led him to go for the full nine-point play. He praised Williams and Goff for their plays, and mentioned that he "just felt good" about the offense's chances to find the end zone.

    The touchdown ended up being a crucial play, and Detroit and Chicago spent much of the second half trading scores. But it wasn't enough to stave off a Bears win.

    According to recent reports, illegal batting, the penalty that sparked the whole sequence, is a relative rarity in the league. One of the only recent examples came against the Lions, with Seattle Seahawks linebacker K.J. Wright batting a fumble out of the end zone in 2015, though the foul was not flagged. The NFL later admitted that the penalty should have been called.

    #211334. Should You Buy Tesla Stock Before December?

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (797 w)
    📖 Baca
    EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Should You Buy Tesla Stock Before December?

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.
    • It has been revealed that tesla (TSLA -1.18%) has had a challenging year.
    • Tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, now leads two publicly traded corporations, the other being Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%), which went public in June.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Tesla ›.

    It has been revealed that tesla (TSLA -1.18%) has had a challenging year. Despite its core electric vehicle (EV) business often performing better than expected, partly due to soaring oil prices, the organization's shares have significantly lagged broader equities. However, the year isn't over, and there is a chance Tesla could finish 2026 with a bang, given ongoing developments. With that stated, should investors consider buying the stock before December?

    Tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, now leads two publicly traded corporations, the other being Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%), which went public in June. Rumors of a potential merger between Tesla and SpaceX have been circulating since before SpaceX was public, but a comment Musk made during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call added fuel to the fire.

    Musk noted that SpaceX and Tesla have formed independent special committees to discuss a potential merger between the two corporations. And more recently, five board directors from both companies have reportedly been discussing a potential all-stock merger that would make the combined entity worth about $3.5 trillion, with a deal possible by year-end. Importantly, this hasn't been confirmed by either company. But it's still worth figuring out the potential benefits and risks of this proposed acquisition.

    Sources indicate that suppose SpaceX acquires Tesla at a 20% premium in an all-stock deal: SpaceX would have to glitch a substantial number of fresh shares, thereby significantly diluting existing shareholders. Tesla's stock might rise, at least initially, while SpaceX's could decline unless investors believe the merger will generate enough synergies to justify the acquisition premium.

    Industry observers note that there are indeed some reasons to think that the combined entity could create more value than either would on its own. For instance, both Tesla and SpaceX are investing massive sums in artificial intelligence (AI). As a single entity, they could eliminate redundant investments and lower costs, while leveraging their larger size to negotiate better deals with suppliers.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Also, some of Tesla's work, including its energy infrastructure and the Optimus humanoid robot, could be of immense value to SpaceX. So, that could be good news for the business' long-term prospects, although whether the proposed combined entity will, on balance, create more value is by no means guaranteed. However, one major source of uncertainty will likely come from regulators. The deal will probably attract significant attention from lawmakers, at least some of whom may try to stop it.

    Recent findings suggest that whether they succeed or not, it's hard to predict the impact on Tesla and SpaceX. And even as a combined entity, the company will be significantly exposed to regulatory risk across businesses such as space launch, satellite-based connectivity, EVs, and robotaxis.

    Putting aside the acquisition talks, Tesla's own business has somewhat attractive prospects. The manufacturer's work in the robotaxi industry looks promising. Tesla introduced the Cybercab, a self-driving vehicle with no steering wheel, no pedals, and no mirrors, earlier this year. Provided it can scale its Cybercab fleet and capture a decent share of the market over the next five to 10 years, the robotaxi business could meaningfully contribute to the company's revenue and profits.

    Recent findings suggest that and Tesla does have an advantage over other robotaxi leaders. The firm has a growing number of subscriptions to its Full Self-Driving software, which it offers to EV owners for $99 per month. A growing FSD ecosystem grants the company access to more data to train and improve its software. And as Tesla has pointed out, the FSD software is becoming one of the reasons people buy Teslas. That's great news for the company's future.

    Sources indicate that but one of Tesla's problems is valuation. At 157.3x forward earnings, the market has already priced in significant success from the company's robotaxi ambition. So, I'd be skeptical about buying Tesla's shares at current levels. I'd prefer a much lower price. The potential merger with SpaceX changes very little, in my view, and actually adds significantly more uncertainty to the mix.

    The combined entity (if a merger does happen) will certainly be worth serious consideration, but investors with an average tolerance for risk and volatility shouldn't buy Tesla stock right now, whether or not they expect the tech giant to merge with SpaceX.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The ongoing earnings season, Middle East tensions and buzz ahead of the U.S. midterm elections have been keeping investors busy. Further, worries about elevated artificial intelligence spending are weighing on investor sentiment.

    Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    This week's first stock pick is Datadog, an AI-powered observability and security platform. The manufacturer will announce its results for the third quarter on Nov. 4. Datadog is seeing strong demand for its offerings, thanks to cloud migration and rapid AI adoption. TipRanks' KPIs tool for DDOG shows the growth in its customer base over the past few years amid increasing market penetration and growing adoption of its products.

    In a recent development, heading into Q3 FY26 earnings, Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda reiterated a buy rating on Datadog stock and raised his price target to $335 from $305. The analyst noted that industry checks and data indicate that infrastructure software demand is strengthening, with AI increasingly driving usage and growth.

    Ikeda called Datadog and Atlassian his top picks, saying that companies that can show that AI is a tailwind to growth could see their valuation rerate, even at premium multiples. He added that the total addressable market for observability is growing faster than anticipated, driven by accelerated growth of enterprise AI and the rapid ramp of consumer AI agents.

    According to recent reports, the five-star analyst believes that focus will be on revenue growth, which he estimates to be 28.7% for Q3 FY26 versus the Street's consensus of 29.1%. Ikeda thinks that the market is underestimating the growth prospects of DDOG's security products. Meanwhile, he cautioned investors about concentration risk related to large customers.

    "We think results will be supportive of our long-term thesis that Datadog is a strong share gainer in the rapidly expanding observability opportunity," said Ikeda.

    Ikeda ranks No. 673 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 55% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.9%. See Datadog Statistics on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that the next pick, semiconductor giant Nvidia, is also benefiting from AI-driven demand for its products. After attending Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reaffirmed a buy rating on NVDA stock with a price target of $300, calling it a top pick in the semiconductor space.

    The five-star analyst mentioned that the conference supported his thesis that Nvidia continues to effectively navigate bottlenecks in the supply chain, land/power/shell, and funding. In fact, Moore is "convinced that all 3 aspects are opportunities for NVDA.".

    It has been revealed that while Nvidia's GTC Berlin offered no major updates, Moore noted the conference reflected that the firm continues to add to its significant advantages heading into 2027. The analyst said that Vera Rubin is gaining momentum, though details on next year's Rubin Ultra were lighter than expected.

    With demand outpacing supply, Moore noted that focus is on closing the gap. In this regard, he highlighted the supply chain deals on substrate, packaging and testing. While the analyst continues to view TSMC 3 nm wafer supply as the biggest challenge, he expects it to ease over time.

    Moore ranks No. 142 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.4%. See Nvidia Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Impressed by the results, Needham analyst Ryan Koontz reiterated a buy rating on SPCX stock with a price target of $250. Koontz highlighted that SpaceX's Q3 results significantly exceeded expectations, proving that the firm's vertically integrated business model is driving massive scale.

    Furthermore, Koontz emphasized the 195.2% sequential growth in SpaceX's AI revenue, fueled by wholesale spot compute deals. He noted management's increasing focus on its AI strategy, given that it is optimistic about adding 10 gigawatts of incremental capacity during 2027.

    "With increasing confidence on Starship re-use, we meaningfully increase our estimates," remarked Koontz.

    Tech Report: Prediction: These 3 Consumer Stocks Will Beat the S&P 500 Over the Next 10 Years

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (755 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that beating the S&P 500 sounds simple until you remember how good the index already is, since it has compounded at about 9.9% a year on a total return basis going back to 1928.
    • It has been revealed that when I look for that kind of staying power in the consumer world, I aim for three things: a brand that people pay up for, a long expansion runway, and a management team that protects both.
    • Ferrari (RACE +2.96%) deliberately builds fewer cars than people want, and that scarcity is the heart of its economic moat, which is a durable advantage that keeps rivals from stealing its customers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Micah Zimmerman – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Ferrari ›.

    Industry observers note that beating the S&P 500 sounds simple until you remember how good the index already is, since it has compounded at about 9.9% a year on a total return basis going back to 1928. So a stock that beats the index over 10 years needs more than a good quarter, it needs a business that can keep growing over the long term.

    It has been revealed that when I look for that kind of staying power in the consumer world, I aim for three things: a brand that people pay up for, a long expansion runway, and a management team that protects both. Here are three consumer stocks that I think long-term investors should consider for the decade ahead.

    Ferrari (RACE +2.96%) deliberately builds fewer cars than people want, and that scarcity is the heart of its economic moat, which is a durable advantage that keeps rivals from stealing its customers.

    CEO Benedetto Vigna said in the third-quarter release that deliveries "reflect our clients' ever-deepening desire to make each Ferrari uniquely their own." Those personal touches add profit to every car without adding volume.

    Demand isn't the problem. Vigna said on the call, "We continue to experience a healthy demand across all geographies, with an order book that enters 2028.".

    The risks are a premium valuation, at roughly 36 times earnings, and the shift to electric models like the Luce, which has to win over buyers who love engines.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Hilton (HLT +0.52%) mostly doesn't own its hotels; it collects fees by managing and licensing its brands to owners through a franchise model, which is an arrangement where a business pays to use another company's brand and systems. That lets it grow without spending heavily on buildings.

    CEO Chris Nassetta said in the third-quarter release, "We achieved our highest quarter ever for organic openings." He also said on the call, "Globally, Hilton is still less than 6% of supply providing a long runway for continued growth.".

    Industry observers note that travel is cyclical, though. CFO Kevin Jacobs said, "RevPAR in China declined 5.4% in the quarter," referring to revenue per available room, which is a key hotel measure of how well rooms are filled and priced. Middle East conflict is weighing on that region, too, and the stock trades near 49 times earnings.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    According to recent reports, amer Sports (AS +2.56%) owns Arc'teryx jackets, Salomon shoes, and Wilson tennis gear, and every segment grew by double digits in its latest quarter. CEO James Zheng said, "I am very confident in the future outlook for our manufacturer".

    The U.S. opportunity is what excites me most. Arc'teryx CEO Stuart Haselden noted that the brand has about as many stores in the U.S. as in Canada, which he noted "makes it very apparent the potential that we have to expand in the U.S." Management also said Europe's store traffic is a challenge, and higher freight costs are nibbling at margins.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Industry observers note that none of these companies will beat the market every year, but I think long-term investors should consider owning all three and giving their growth stories the full decade they deserve. Great brands tend to compound quietly.

    What ties these three together is pricing power, which is the ability to raise prices without losing customers, and I think that matters more over a decade than any single quarter's results.

    Ferrari's buyers wait years for their cars, Hilton's owners keep signing up for its brands, and Arc'teryx shoppers happily pay premium prices for gear that lasts.

    It has been revealed that there will be rough stretches, whether it's a travel slowdown, a weak luxury market, or a cold winter for outdoor sales, but investors who hold through those dips give each business time to prove its case. In the end, patience is the edge most investors give up too easily.

    By Daniel Foelber – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) investors have been on a rather unenjoyable roller coaster in recent weeks. And every time the ride looks like it's nearing an end, there's another unexpected turn that unearths more questions than answers.

    Industry observers note that founder and CEO for over 33 years, Jensen Huang, admitted on Nov. 8 to being unfaithful to his wife, then resigned on Nov. 12, only to be brought back as CEO less than two weeks later on Nov. 23.

    According to recent reports, that same day, President Trump was on a phone interview with CNBC and took credit for speaking with Nvidia's board and helping convince them to bring Huang back. Trump remarked, "I spoke to them. Let me just put it that way. And I convinced them. And I will tell you, it was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago." Trump was referring to Nvidia's stock price and how it was easier to convince Nvidia to bring Huang back when the stock was cratering.

    Nvidia has rallied substantially since Huang came back as CEO, but Huang and Nvidia still face an uphill climb of federal, state, and internal investigations linked to Nvidia misleading investors and potential national security violations regarding advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence (AI) chips leaking into China through backdoor channels.

    It has been revealed that the stock is still under $100 per share at the time of this writing and down 20% year to date -- making it the worst-performing "Magnificent Seven" stock in 2026. The Magnificent Seven consists of seven mega-cap tech-focused companies that include Nvidia, Apple (AAPL +0.43%), Microsoft (MSFT -1.25%), Alphabet (GOOG -2.02%) (GOOGL -2.13%), Amazon (AMZN -3.12%), Meta Platforms (META +3.40%), and Tesla (TSLA -1.18%).

    Here's the simplest reason to buy Nvidia, and an argument for why it's best to keep the semiconductor stock on a watch list for now.

    Heading into this year, some investors were concerned that Nvidia would be unable to maintain its breakneck revenue growth rate and high gross margins. But hyperscalers continued to ramp up AI capital expenditures. And Nvidia has broadened its customer base to other enterprises, AI start-ups, AI labs, and neoclouds.

    As a result, Nvidia's earnings growth began outpacing its stock price growth, compressing its valuation. But then the unthinkable happened.

    It has been revealed that nvidia's stock price has plummeted despite exceptional results and guidance for 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028. Nvidia reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 17, with revenue more than doubling from the third quarter of fiscal 2026. In the nine months ended Oct. 25, 2026, Nvidia generated $183.3 billion in net income compared to $77.11 billion for the nine months ended Oct. 26, 2025.

    Nvidia is on track to surpass Alphabet as the world's most profitable company. It now trades at just 15.4 times forward earnings -- making it the cheapest Magnificent Seven stock despite having the highest gross margins and the fastest revenue growth rate.

    TSLA PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

    For context, the forward P/E of the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) is 17.3 -- meaning Nvidia is now priced like a value stock.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Sources indicate that buying high-quality companies on sale is an excellent way to compound wealth over time. Nvidia doesn't have to deliver blowout results to impress investors. In fact, its growth rate could fall substantially, and it would still be a steal at current levels.

    The issue isn't Nvidia's valuation -- it's investors' concerns about where the company could be headed over the next three to five years.

    Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang's sudden resignation exposed Nvidia's extreme vulnerability to key-person risk, governance failures, and an incapable board of directors. Going forward, Nvidia will need to change its structure to be less dependent on Huang, which could make it more rigid and less innovative but also protect long-term investors.

    In addition to Nvidia-specific problems, there's also the risk that AI spending could decline considerably due to higher interest rates, which have made borrowing more expensive. With democrats taking control of the Senate and the House, there may be higher regulatory hurdles to accelerating data center construction. And there's the ongoing risk that compute demand will taper off as AI models become more efficient.

    Granted, Nvidia is incredibly well positioned to endure a slowdown because of its industry-leading position and rock solid balance sheet. But it could also lead to stagnating or declining earnings in the medium term, which would challenge Nvidia's valuation.

    Recent findings suggest that all told, Nvidia simply has too many unknowns right now. Until investors get more clarity on the findings of the investigations, the company's succession strategy for Huang, and the extent of its governance overhaul, Nvidia remains a hold.

    Heading into the new year, I'd rather buy high-quality Magnificent Seven stocks with a clear runway for future earnings growth like Alphabet, even if its valuation is more expensive than Nvidia's.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:47PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Legend Biotech ›.

    In a recent development, on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, Legend Biotech (LEGN -0.23%) announced that net trade sales for CARVYKTI, its cell therapy for multiple myeloma, a blood cancer, grew 36% year over year to $710 million. Adoption in earlier lines of cancer treatment and improved manufacturing efficiency are driving the business toward full-year profitability. Three things management remarked stand out.

    Second- and third-line patients reached 50% of U.S. apheresis volume, the blood-cell collection process required to manufacture CARVYKTI, up from 41% earlier in the year. It's getting patients onto therapy at first relapse, which improves clinical outcomes and expands the addressable market before competing treatments take hold.

    Gross margin, the portion of sales remaining after direct production expenses, reached 58% in the third quarter, driven by manufacturing gains. Operating income reached $46.8 million, which includes a $24 million one-time credit related to share-based compensation. It's on track for full-year profitability on an adjusted net income basis, a non-IFRS accounting metric that excludes non-recurring charges.

    Recent findings suggest that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration cleared the Investigational Upcoming Drug application, or IND, for LB2501, Legend Biotech's in vivo cell therapy that genetically modifies white blood cells directly inside a patient. It's seeing early clinical success, with a 100% overall and complete response rates at dose level 2.

    Industry observers note that international expansion is accelerating across 20 markets, and updated treatment guidelines favor cell therapy before antibody treatments. Management is keeping a close eye on doctor referral patterns and manufacturing capacity as overseas sales scale up.

    A deep cash cushion provides strategic flexibility as clinical trials evaluate earlier treatment settings and next-generation platforms. That balance sheet strength allows the business to scale production and fund research without taking on debt.
